## Satis Appraisal v0.3.0

This release merges everything the hourly improvement loop has landed since v0.2.4 —
five audited cycles, each committed only after an adversarial review approved it, with
every fix proven by a test that failed first. The test suite grows from 251 to 300 tests
and the in-app financial audit from 61 to 66 checks.

### Every screen now prices the same, repaired scheme
- **One appraisal entry point.** The Options grid and the Pricing brief used to price the
  *raw* project file inside a bare `catch {}`, while only the Appraisal page sanitised the
  inputs. A mistyped bridge rate (450% pa) produced **-£7,365,660 on an option card against
  +£431,604 on the Appraisal page for the same option** — a £7.8m sign flip between two
  screens showing one scheme. All three views now run through a single `appraiseProject`
  pipeline that repairs the spec, reports every repair it applied, and never throws; a
  failed run says what failed and what was repaired instead of reading "No option
  selected yet".
- **The research brief is built from the repaired figures.** The finance-research agent was
  being asked to price bridge terms at a raw 700% LTV against a facility sized at the
  clamped 100%. It now reads entirely from the repaired spec.

### Corrupt project files can no longer silently reprice a scheme
- **Every discriminant input is validated.** `buildCostMode`, `vat.fundedBy`,
  `waterfall.mode` and `sdlt.regime` are each repaired (and the repair disclosed) rather
  than silently taking a fallback branch. A corrupt `buildCostMode` previously *added
  £251,748 of profit* with zero repairs reported and a green 65-check audit; a corrupt
  `waterfall.mode` quietly dropped three audit checks and paid the wrong split.
- **Duplicate cost-line codes are rejected.** A duplicated cost line swung net profit from
  **+£779,615 to -£1,671,760 without a single audit fail**. The sanitiser now de-duplicates
  by code, reports each dropped copy, and a new auditor tripwire fails any spec still
  carrying a repeat.
- **A loss-making waterfall is now audited as one.** The auditor's reconciliation gate
  disagreed with the engine's about when a waterfall degrades to a pro-rata split, so a
  loss-making waterfall lost three checks exactly when scrutiny mattered.

### Investor returns on an honest denominator
- **ROI is reported on both committed and drawn capital.** The same deal used to report
  the same investor profit as 18.75% in simple mode and 24.67% in waterfall mode — a
  5.9-point swing on a presentation switch, because the two modes silently used different
  capital bases. The waterfall now reports committed and drawn-peak capital for investor
  and developer separately, ROI on each basis plus per-annum equivalents, and the audit
  reconciles the capital bases in every profit scenario.

### An unbuildable option no longer wears a compliance badge
- **Zero-dwelling options are not "NDSS compliant".** An envelope too shallow to plan a
  single dwelling was vacuously passing every space-standard check and showing a green
  compliance badge beside £0 of GDV — and its card printed the sunk cost of building
  nothing as if it were an appraisal. It now reads "Not viable — no dwellings".

### Under the hood
- The improvement loop's own tooling ships in the repo: `scripts/loop-status.sh` reports
  loop progress from any checkout, and a preflight refuses cycles on stranded, stale or
  already-built work.
- Saved projects open unchanged: repairs disclose, they do not re-price — for each new
  validation the fallback is the branch the engine already took, and the golden regression
  pins in `tests/dcf.test.ts` have not moved. Figures remain **pre-tax** throughout.
